step0_classification.evidence: The core switch fans two links into the application tier (core->web 10 GbE, core->cache 25 GbE) and the three application nodes close a triangle (web->cache session, web->db queries, cache->db fill), so the graph is a fan around a core with mesh relations, not a chain (density: 7 relations over 6 nodes) and not a fabric (no redundant parallel links, no double arrowheads).
tie_breakers_considered: Density wins over depth: 7 edges > 6 nodes, so not flow-chains even though wan->fw->core is a straight run.
No disconnected worlds and no source-named bus, so not placement-planes.
No addresses, ports or qualifier markers, so not identity-probe-maps.
Motion is a signature, not a tie-breaker: the source asks for live flowing dots, but the fan shape (2 out of core, in-source order web then cache) is what decides the family.
step0_classification.secondary_recipe: flow-chains only for the transit hop inside v1 (wan->fw->core kept as one short 4-rank lr run with one stage per rank, so each hop label owns its own corridor).
step0_classification.anti_parallel_pair: none exists in the source: all 7 relations are one-directional (wen->fw 1 GbE, fw->core 10 GbE, core->web 10 GbE, core->cache 25 GbE, web->cache session, web->db queries, cache->db fill). The mesh recipe's pair clause was therefore not triggered; no reverse edge was invented to satisfy it.
